newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares mixed early, blue chips sought.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares mixed early, blue chips sought.

text.p: Singapore share opened mixed on Friday as investors placed small bets on blue chips ahead of expected positive May non-oil export data, dealers said.
The outlook remained cautious with punting opportunities still scarce and institutions reducing exposure.
The Straits Times Industrials Index rose at the outset but then slipped 2.17 points to 2,000.08 at mid-morning. Dealers said it threatened to break the psychological 2,000-point level.
Van der Horst shares pared sharp losses by rising Singapore $0.13 to S$2.71 at 0215 GMT after its chairman denied rumours on Thursday of having severed ties with the company.
He also denied the engineering-based company had lost interest in doing business in Singapore.
SIA foreign shares were unmoved by the announcement of a four-airline alliance with Air New Zealand, Ansett Australia and Ansett International.
The share was at S$12.20, unchanged from late Thurday.
Some nibbling was seen in small capitalisation stocks, with Excel Machine hitting a new high of S$0.71, up one cent.
Meanwhile, a Reuter poll forecast a 3.5 percent rise on year for May's non-oil exports, the second consecutive rise after five months of falls.
